title: Behold the Lofty Sky
description: Behold the Lofty Sky in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 19, part 1, headed “The book of nature and scripture”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold the lof-ty sky De-clares its mak-er God, And all his star-ry works on high Pro-claim his power a-broad.

lines: And all his starry works on high
Still keep their course the same;
While night to day, and day to night
They shew the wonders of his hand,
We are not left to nature's voice
To bid us know the Lord.
He puts his gospel in our hands,
His laws are just and pure,
Nor gold that has the furnace past
While of thy works I sing,
Accept the praise, my God, my King,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
